newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bavarian bank confirms large credit for Kirch.
newsitem.headline: Bavarian bank confirms large credit for Kirch.

text.p: A bank controlled by the Bavarian state government confirmed on Monday it was leading a group that planned to provide a large credit line to the Kirch Group media concern.
The Landesanstalt fuer Aufbaufinanzierung (LfA) would provide several hundred million marks in credit to Kirch, a spokesman told Reuters on Monday.

The Sueddeutsche Zeitung newspaper reported earlier on Monday that LfA would provide 500 million marks ($295.6 million) in credits to Kirch, which is struggling to get a costly digital television venture off the ground.
Private banks would contribute additional credits to bring the total to well over one billion marks, the newspaper said.

Kirch has been seeking a partner for its DSF 1 digital TV channel, which has only won 30,000 customers since its launch several months ago. Earlier in March Australian media magnate Rupert Murdoch gave up plans to joint DSF 1, which Kirch expected to have 700,000 customers at the end of 1997.

Kirch, which owns a huge library of films and TV programmes and has the rights to broadcast the soccer World Cup in 2002 and 2006, has invested in satellite services, decoders and other digital technology for DSF 1.
